No Revisit dates have passed yet. The next one is bake-to-order on 2 December.

## Doubling in 30 days isn't realistic, and you'd hit capacity first

Going from 140 to 280 subscribers means about 140 new signups in a month. You got 15 in October, so that's roughly 9 times your current rate. The bigger problem is Saturday. Your no-trial record says Saturday delivery slots are already your limit, so 280 boxes on one morning, with 3 people and cargo bikes, would probably break delivery before marketing does.

My recommendation is to aim for **+40 to 60 paying subscribers in 30 days**. That's 3 to 4 times your current rate. Before you spend anything, work out your real Saturday ceiling: how many boxes per bike run, how many runs fit before about 10 am, and how much the oven can bake. If the ceiling is around 200, that's your actual target.

## What I'd do (about €300)

**1. Referral push to existing subscribers (week 1, about €100)**
Your 140 subscribers already live inside the 3 km radius and like the bread, so they're your best channel. Give each of them a card in Saturday's box with "Give a friend 50% off their first month, and you get a free loaf." The 50% offer for new customers was discarded on 6 October, but its reopen condition is "test it with a referral from an existing subscriber." This is that test, so it fits your rules. Track the results so you can decide whether to keep it.

**2. Christmas gift subscriptions (start now, runs to 24 December)**
Sell 4-week and 8-week gift boxes, paid in full upfront, with a printed card. It's well timed and you get the cash in advance. Recipients are already paying customers when the gift ends, so it's not a free trial, and the conversion pitch is "keep it going." Promote it in the shop, in the boxes and on a sign on the bikes.

**3. Street-by-street density (weeks 1 to 4, about €120)**
Put flyers in letterboxes on the streets you already deliver to: "Your neighbours at no. 12 and 18 get fresh bread every Saturday." Each new subscriber on an existing route costs almost no extra delivery time, which protects your Saturday capacity. Add a QR code that goes straight to paid signup.

**4. Convert walk-in customers (no cost)**
Everyone who buys at the counter gets asked "Do you live within 3 km?" and is handed a signup card. With a 3-person team, this is the cheapest acquisition you have.

**5. Offices and shared buildings within 3 km (about €80 for samples and printing)**
Pitch a Friday or Saturday office box, or one drop for a whole apartment building. You get many subscribers for one stop.

## Off the table (your ledger)

- **Free trial or free first box.** Discarded on 6 October: 6 of 52 converted, and the free boxes used up Saturday slots. Reopen only if paid signups fall below 8 a month for 2 months in a row. October had 15, so the condition isn't met.
- **Delivery apps or a courier partner to handle the volume.** Discarded on 18 August. Delivery apps take 30% commission and you lose contact with the customer. A courier was €4.50 per drop. Reopen only if you open a second shop (apps) or pass 300 subscribers (courier).

## Tracking

Each week, record signups by source (referral, gift, flyer, walk-in, office), the referral conversion rate, and Saturday delivery time. If Saturday rounds go past your cutoff, stop acquiring and start a waitlist.

If you go ahead with the referral test or the gift subscriptions, tell me and I'll log them in the ledger.
